prompt: Why does the `**` route go last?

choices.text: Angular refuses a wildcard anywhere else
choices.why: It is accepted anywhere; it just matches everything.

choices.text: The router takes the first match
choices.why: Right. First, it would answer every address.

choices.text: So that it loads after the other components
choices.why: Order decides matching, not loading.

choices.text: It must be the last import in the file
choices.why: Imports have nothing to do with it.
It sets it; it changes nothing about it.

choices.text: It adds a `courseId` input to the component
choices.why: The input was already there, since lesson 8.

choices.text: It sets the input from the parameter
choices.why: Right. The component did not change.

choices.text: It reloads the course when the page loads
choices.why: The store loads the data; the router sets an input.

prompt: `curl -si http://localhost:4200/courses/git` answered `200 OK`. Why, with no such file?

choices.why: Right. Then the router decides.

prompt: The component for the current address is drawn where the template has `<___ />`.

prompt: Why was `exact: true` needed on the link to `/`?

choices.text: Without it, the link would not navigate
choices.why: It would navigate; the question is when it counts as active.
It is valid.
The redirect handles `/week`.

prompt: After the links arrived, three tests failed with `NG0201` for `ActivatedRoute`. Why?

jsdom has one; the error was about injection.

choices.text: The tests ran before the dev server
choices.why: Tests do not use the dev server.

prompt: `/courses/rust` showed "There is no course called rust." What happened?

prompt: Old code reads `route.snapshot.paramMap.get('courseId')` in `ngOnInit`. What goes wrong going from one course to another?

choices.text: The router reloads the page, losing the data
choices.why: The router does not reload the page.

prompt: Match each way of getting `courseId` with whether it follows a change of course.
Where is a child route's component drawn?

choices.why: The parent stays; the child goes inside it.
Right. `CoursePage` has one.

choices.text: In a dialog over the page
choices.why: Routes draw into outlets, not dialogs.
Beside would need a second outlet in `App`.
The parent's own route has the parameter.

choices.text: So that redirects keep their parameters
choices.why: Redirects use their own route's parameters.

choices.text: To share the store between children
choices.why: The store is in the root; routes do not decide that.

prompt: Why does it matter that the address bar shows the new address after a redirect?

choices.text: The router needs it to draw the page
choices.why: It drew the page from the match.

choices.text: The old address would otherwise stop working
choices.why: The redirect keeps it working either way.

prompt: Why should every route set a title?

choices.text: The router refuses routes without one
choices.why: A title is optional to the router.

choices.text: It makes the page load faster
choices.why: It changes one line of the document.
